title: The Rwandan genocide
subject: histoire
description: In **100 days**, between April and July **1994**, hundreds of thousands of Tutsis and moderate Hutus were massacred in Rwanda. The fastest genocide of the century is taking place before the eyes of the world.

hero.hook: One hundred days. Hundreds of thousands of deaths. And a world that chose not to intervene.

blocks.text: Between April and July **1994**, in just **100 days**, Rwanda experienced a tragedy of rare density in history. Between **500,000** and **800,000** Tutsis, as well as moderate Hutus, are systematically murdered.
This genocide is notable for its speed and the inaction of the international community. Understanding 1994 means understanding colonial roots, political planning, and diplomatic silence.

In Rwanda, Hutus (approximately **85%**) and Tutsis (approximately **14%**) did not form, before colonization, fixed “races”. The distinction was above all social and economic: a Hutu enriched with livestock could become a Tutsi, and vice versa.
In **1933**, the Belgian administration fixed membership on the **ethnic identity card**. We sometimes classify according to the shape of the nose… or the number of cows: beyond ten, we are Tutsi.

The Belgian settlers, influenced by racial theories, first relied on the Tutsis, then turned to the Hutu majority as independence approached (**1962**). Pogroms push thousands of Tutsis into exile. Hate becomes inheritance.

In the 1990s, President **Juvénal Habyarimana** led the country. His regime is at war with the [[Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF)]], made up of Tutsi exiles. The [[Hutu Power]] extremists form the Interahamwe militias. The [[Radio des Mille Collines]] spreads hatred and dehumanizes Tutsis every day.

blocks.caption: Rwanda in 1994, scene of a planned genocide.

blocks.text: **April 6, 1994**, the presidential plane was shot down. Within the hour, the dams close. Around **8,000** people are killed every day. The massacre is local: neighbors, colleagues, local authorities. This is not a spontaneous explosion. It's an organized operation.

On site, , the UN mission commanded by Canadian Roméo Dallaire, only has an observation mandate. Traumatized by the failure in , the United States slowed down any intervention. We even avoid the word “genocide”, which would require action in accordance with the 1948 Convention. [[UNAMIR and General Dallaire]] [[Somalia]]

blocks.caption: Paul Kagame and the FPR, whose offensive puts an end to the massacres.

blocks.text: France belatedly launched Operation , officially humanitarian, but controversial for having facilitated the flight of genocidaires to , the current Democratic Republic of Congo. It is not the UN which stops the killings: it is the RPF offensive, led by **Paul Kagame**, which takes Kigali, the capital, on **July 4, 1994**. [[Turquoise]] [[Zaire]]

After July 1994, the country must judge the unjustifiable. The [[Gacaca]] courts, neighborhood courts, handle nearly two million cases. The [[International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR)]] judges the great planners. The Kigali memorial houses more than **250, 000** victims.

blocks.text: In **100 days** (1994), hundreds of thousands of Tutsis were murdered in Rwanda. Despite the warnings, the world does not intervene; only the RPF offensive stopped the genocide.
